seo.title: Pump Flow Calculator - Q from Power
seo.description: Pump Flow Calculator — Calculate pump flow rate from power, head, and efficiency using the hydraulic power formula with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Q = P_shaft × η / (ρgH). P_shaft in W (engine converts kW→W); ×3600 converts m³/s to m³/h.

content.introduction: Calculate the flow rate a pump will deliver given its shaft power, efficiency, and the system head. This inverts the standard hydraulic power equation to solve for Q.

example.description: 15 kW pump at 75% efficiency pumping water to 40m head delivers ~103 m³/h.

faq.a: It gives rated flow at a specific operating point. Actual flow depends on where the pump curve intersects the system curve.

faq.q: Why does flow decrease as head increases?
faq.a: Centrifugal pumps have a falling head-flow curve. At higher system resistance (more head), less flow can be produced for the same power.

faq.q: How do I convert flow between m³/h and gpm?
faq.a: 1 m³/h = 4.403 US gpm. For example, 50 m³/h = 220 gpm. Conversely, divide gpm by 4.403 to get m³/h. 1 m³/h also equals 0.2778 L/s.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Pump Flow
sections.body:
**Flow rate units**

- 1 m³/h = 0.2778 L/s = 4.403 US gpm
- 1 US gpm = 0.2271 m³/h = 3.785 L/min
- 1 L/s = 3.6 m³/h

**Volume units**

- 1 m³ = 1000 L = 264.17 US gal

Pump flow is the volumetric rate at the pump suction conditions. Convert all flow inputs to one consistent unit before applying the pump curve or affinity laws.
